fatal_errors: The proposed HPHT treatment is unrelated to the intermediate-temperature aging treatment responsible for the target transition.
The hypothesis predicts simultaneous strength–ductility enhancement rather than a non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
It does not identify the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA or its as-cast FCC+B2 state.
The stated deformation mechanism omits enhanced L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and phase-boundary stress concentration.
The proposed temperature range up to 1600°C does not reproduce the approximately 550–750°C brittle window or the 600°C ductility minimum and 750°C recovery.
The cited evidence concerns HPHT strength–ductility synergy, generic HEA properties, and damping alloys, not aging-induced temper embrittlement in the target alloy.
explanation: The response recognizes only the broad relevance of eutectic high-entropy alloys and interface-controlled deformation. It otherwise addresses a different materials problem: HPHT-induced strength–ductility synergy. It neither reconstructs the alloy-specific aging protocol nor explains the observed ductile–brittle–ductile sequence. Its falsification experiment tests whether HPHT improves strength and ductility, so even a positive result would not discriminate or validate the target transition. The evidence may support some generic statements about HEAs and HPHT processing, but it is not probative for the question asked.
